thread:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — I found a base64 blob in partner-ingest logs that looks like a KMS-wrapped ciphertext fragment. Not confident it's complete header. Pinging @Maya @Jon @Priya for triage. Sample line: `ingest: user=partner-23 payload=YmFzZTY0X3dhcHBlZF9jaXBoZXJ0ZXh0X19mcmFncg==`

Maya Singh: can you paste the full line and which host/stream?

Alex Chen: host: ingest-03.prod, stream: partner-webhooks. Full context: `2026-03-21T14:12:31Z ingest webhook id=abc123 partner=acme payload="YmFzZTY0X3dhcHBlZF9jaXBoZXJ0ZXh0X19mcmFncg=="` — looks truncated (no metadata prefix like `vault:v1:`).

Jon R.: thanks. first quick checks: 1) search for the same blob across other streams 2) check Vault audit for any decrypt/unwrap ops around that time 3) temporarily revoke the partner ingestion token if it's still valid.

Sam W.: running grep across s3 log-buckets now, will report hits.

devops-bot: grep results: 3 matches across ingest-01..03 between 2026-03-21T14:10..14:18Z (IDs: abc123, def456, ghi789).

Maya Singh: @security-bot — can you pull Vault audit entries for transit unwrap/rewrap for keys: `transit/redwood-wrap` and `transit/partner-wrap` between 14:00..15:00Z? Also check KMS proxy logs for rewrap requests.

security-bot: vault-audit: no explicit unwrap requests for those ciphertexts found. KMS-proxy: 2 requests in that window from svc-ingest (ip 10.4.2.9) but both returned 4xx (invalid-ciphertext).

Priya Patel: hypothesis: partner sent a partial chunk or our logging captured a trimmed payload before the client added metadata. Blast radius: likely only partner webhook ingestion. But assume worst — treat as potential exposure of wrapped blobs. Recommended immediate actions: rotate wrapping key, create ephemeral replacement SA for partner, enable targeted audit-forwarding to SIEM, and scrub logs.

Alex Chen: agree. propose timeline: T+0:30m — revoke partner API key; T+2h — rotate wrap key; T+4h — rewrap secrets and restart dependent services; T+24h — run audit & postmortem.

Jon R.: operational steps I can do now:
- [ ] revoke partner API key (I will do now)
- [ ] update RBAC to deny any write from svc-ingest to `secret/partner/*` until we confirm
- [ ] schedule rewrap job for affected mounts after new key is active

Jon R.: revoke command run: `gcloud secrets versions destroy --secret=partner-api-key --version=latest --project=infra-prod` (we archived current key and created rotate token). Partner notified via email.

Sam W.: grep found the same base64 string in three places; all were < 100 bytes. Suggest log-scrub for future: mask base64-looking payloads in helm values for ingest service.

Maya Singh: +1. I'll open a PR to Kyverno policy to block/replace long base64 fields in logs/annotations. Patch notes: add mutate rule to mask `request.body` if matches `^([A-Za-z0-9+/]{80,}={0,2})$`.

Priya Patel: rewrap plan (high level): rotate transit key `transit/redwood-wrap` -> create new key version, then run rewrap endpoint to re-encrypt ciphertexts under new key. Example Vault API (for reference):
```
curl -sS --header "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  --request POST \
  --data '{"ciphertext": "<old-ciphertext>"}' \
  https://vault.preprod.internal/v1/transit/rewrap/transit/redwood-wrap
```
Note: our proxy may be `redwood-kms-proxy` which uses a slightly different path. Jon, confirm which path we use in prod.

Jon R.: prod uses vault internal path `/v1/transit/rewrap/redwood-wrap`. I'll validate with a dry-run on staging first.

Maya Singh: also: add SIEM alert rule to flag any raw base64 > 64 chars in webhook payloads. Create a temporary SIEM dashboard for affected partner.

Alex Chen: who will own the rewrap? Assignments: Jon -> run rotate + rewrap job; Priya -> coordinate audit logs & SIEM; Maya -> kyverno/log-scrub PR; Sam -> scrub logs and S3 lifecycle to remove captures; Alex -> communications with partner & exec update.

Jon R.: starting key rotate in 20m on staging. ETA for prod: 2h after we validate. Rewrap job is idempotent; will kick off with concurrency 4.

Priya Patel: I'm pulling CloudTrail and Vault audit logs into the incident folder (s3://redwood-incidents/3770004321/). Also enabling 90-day retention for these logs in SIEM.

Sam W.: begun scrubbing S3 objects matching `*partner-webhooks*` — copying originals to secure-archive and replacing with masked versions.

Alex Chen: thumbs up. Once rotate+rewrap complete, let's run spot-checks: decrypt a few rewrapped blobs in staging and verify app can fetch secrets.

security-bot: checklist summary created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3770004321 (automated)

Maya Singh: PR for kyverno policy opened: https://git.internal/kyverno/policies/merge_requests/42 (includes unit tests).

Jon R.: PROD rotate done at 16:25Z. Rewrap job started 16:32Z. So far 412 objects rewrapped, 0 failures.

Alex Chen: good. Priya — when can we have a short blameless postmortem?

Priya Patel: I'll draft an outline tonight. Postmortem + remediation + timeline due EOD tomorrow.

Alex Chen: closing checklist once postmortem is posted and SIEM alert remains firing for 24h. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
